claim: AMATERAS-2 is a volumetric trans-scale imaging system with an ultra-large field-of-view that enables simultaneous observation of millions of cellular dynamics in centimeter-wide three-dimensional tissues and embryos.
source: We established a volumetric trans-scale imaging system with an ultra-large field-of-view (FOV) that enables simultaneous observation of millions of cellular dynamics in centimeter-wide three-dimensional (3D) tissues and embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as the main achievement of the study.

claim: AMATERAS-2 uses a custom-made giant lens system with a magnification of ×2 and a numerical aperture (NA) of 0.25.
source: Using a custom-made giant lens system with a magnification of ×2 and a numerical aperture (NA) of 0.25, and a CMOS camera with more than 100 megapixels, we built a trans-scale scope AMATERAS-2
evidence: The specifications of the lens system are directly stated in the abstract.

claim: AMATERAS-2 realizes fluorescence imaging with a transverse spatial resolution of approximately 1.1 µm across an FOV of approximately 1.5×1.0 cm2.
source: we built a trans-scale scope AMATERAS-2, and realized fluorescence imaging with a transverse spatial resolution of approximately 1.1 µm across an FOV of approximately 1.5×1.0 cm2.
evidence: The spatial resolution and FOV are explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: The 3D resolving capability of AMATERAS-2 was realized through a combination of optical and computational sectioning techniques tailored for the low-power imaging system.
source: The 3D resolving capability was realized through a combination of optical and computational sectioning techniques tailored for our low-power imaging system.
evidence: The methods used to achieve 3D imaging are stated in the abstract.

claim: AMATERAS-2 was applied to a 1.2 cm-wide section of mouse brain and successfully observed various regions with sub-cellular resolution in a single FOV.
source: We applied the imaging technique to 1.2 cm-wide section of mouse brain, and successfully observed various regions of the brain with sub-cellular resolution in a single FOV.
evidence: This application is described in the abstract as a demonstration of the system's capabilities.

claim: Time-lapse imaging of a 1-cm-wide vascular network during quail embryo development was performed for over 24 hr, visualizing the movement of over 4.0×10^5 vascular endothelial cells.
source: We also performed time-lapse imaging of a 1-cm-wide vascular network during quail embryo development for over 24 hr, visualizing the movement of over 4.0×105 vascular endothelial cells and quantitatively analyzing their dynamics.
evidence: This experimental result is stated in the abstract.

claim: Multicellular systems are generally complex, comprising heterogeneous cells rather than homogeneous assemblies.
source: Multicellular systems are generally complex, comprising heterogeneous cells rather than homogeneous assemblies.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the introduction.

claim: To understand the mechanism by which numerous cells cooperate to express the function of the entire system, it is ideal to observe all individual components within the system simultaneously during the time span of a whole phenomenon.
source: To understand the mechanism by which numerous cells cooperate to express the function of the entire system, it is ideal to observe all individual components within the system simultaneously during the time span of a whole phenomenon.
evidence: This is stated as a scientific rationale in the introduction.

claim: In scenarios where a small fraction of cells in a large multicellular system may influence the fate of the population, or when distant cells and tissues operate synchronously, deducing the entire system from observations of sub-populations becomes challenging.
source: In particular, in scenarios where a small fraction of cells in a large multicellular system may influence the fate of the population, or when distant cells and tissues operate synchronously, deducing the entire system from observations of sub-populations becomes challenging.
evidence: This is stated as a scientific challenge in the introduction.

claim: Researchers have recently reported the development of imaging methods with large field-of-view.
source: In response to this demand, researchers have recently reported the development of imaging methods with large field-of-view (FOV; McConnell et al., 2016; Sofroniew et al., 2016; Fan et al., 2019; Ota et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2021; Ichimura et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Most large FOV imaging methods are focused on observing brain activity in neuroscience using two-photon excited fluorescence.
source: Whereas most of these methods are focused on observing brain activity in neuroscience using two-photon excited fluorescence (Sofroniew et al., 2016; Fan et al., 2019; Ota et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2021)
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: AMATERAS-1 was a fluorescence imaging system for the visible wavelength region, capable of spatially resolving individual cells within a centimeter FOV, enabling simultaneous observation of dynamics in the range of 10^5–10^6 cells.
source: In our previous work, we proposed a fluorescence imaging system for the visible wavelength region, capable of spatially resolving individual cells within a centimeter FOV, which we named AMATERAS-1 (A Multi-scale/modal Analytical Tool for Every Rare Activity in Singularity), enabling simultaneous observation of dynamics in the range of 105–106 cells (Ichimura et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the predecessor system with citation.

claim: AMATERAS-1 successfully detected less than 1% of cells with unique roles in multicellular systems and revealed how these rare cells trigger a drastic transition from unicellular to multicellular behavior in Dictyostelium discoideum.
source: Additionally, we successfully detected less than 1% of cells with unique roles in multicellular systems and revealed how these rare cells trigger a drastic transition from unicellular to multicellular behavior in Dictyostelium discoideum (Kakizuka et al., 2025).
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding with citation.

claim: AMATERAS-1 had a numerical aperture (NA) of 0.12, which is insufficient for realizing volumetric observation owing to its broad depth of field.
source: However, the imaging system had a numerical aperture (NA) of 0.12, which is insufficient for realizing volumetric observation owing to its broad depth of field (DOF).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the previous system.

claim: The objective lens of AMATERAS-2 is composed of 12 optical elements in 7 groups.
source: The objective lens is composed of 12 optical elements in 7 groups, while the tube lens is composed of 9 lenses in 6 groups (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The tube lens of AMATERAS-2 is composed of 9 lenses in 6 groups.
source: The objective lens is composed of 12 optical elements in 7 groups, while the tube lens is composed of 9 lenses in 6 groups (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Both the objective and tube lenses are infinity-corrected with NAs of 0.25 for the objective and 0.125 for the tube lens.
source: Both lenses are infinity-corrected with NAs of 0.25 for the objective and 0.125 for the tube lens, and have a field number of 44 mm (diameter) suitable for large-area image sensors.
evidence: The optical specifications are explicitly stated.

claim: The lenses have a field number of 44 mm (diameter) suitable for large-area image sensors.
source: Both lenses are infinity-corrected with NAs of 0.25 for the objective and 0.125 for the tube lens, and have a field number of 44 mm (diameter) suitable for large-area image sensors.
evidence: The field number is explicitly stated.

claim: The lenses are effectively aberration-corrected to the diffraction limit or lower in the visible wavelength range of 436–656 nm.
source: They are effectively aberration-corrected to the diffraction limit or lower in the visible wavelength range of 436–656 nm.
evidence: The aberration correction performance is stated.

claim: The objective lens has dimensions of 144 mm × 310 mm.
source: The objective lens and tube lens have sizes of 144 mm × 310 mm and 170 mm × 345 mm, respectively (Figure 1B).
evidence: The dimensions are stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The tube lens has dimensions of 170 mm × 345 mm.
source: The objective lens and tube lens have sizes of 144 mm × 310 mm and 170 mm × 345 mm, respectively (Figure 1B).
evidence: The dimensions are stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The objective and tube lenses exhibit zero vignetting, enabling observation of peripheral areas of the FOV with high brightness.
source: The objective and tube lenses exhibit zero vignetting, enabling observation of peripheral areas of the FOV with high brightness.
evidence: The optical performance characteristic is stated.

claim: As the NA of AMATERAS-2 is 0.25, more than double that of AMATERAS-1 (0.12), the system in principle achieves over twice the spatial resolution in the transverse (xy) direction.
source: As the NA of AMATERAS-2 is 0.25, more than double that of AMATERAS-1 (0.12), our system in principle achieves over twice the spatial resolution in the transverse (xy) direction, more than four times the resolution in the longitudinal (z) direction, and over four times the brightness of AMATERAS-1.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical improvement based on optical principles.

claim: AMATERAS-2 achieves more than four times the resolution in the longitudinal (z) direction compared to AMATERAS-1.
source: As the NA of AMATERAS-2 is 0.25, more than double that of AMATERAS-1 (0.12), our system in principle achieves over twice the spatial resolution in the transverse (xy) direction, more than four times the resolution in the longitudinal (z) direction, and over four times the brightness of AMATERAS-1.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical improvement based on optical principles.

claim: AMATERAS-2 achieves over four times the brightness of AMATERAS-1.
source: As the NA of AMATERAS-2 is 0.25, more than double that of AMATERAS-1 (0.12), our system in principle achieves over twice the spatial resolution in the transverse (xy) direction, more than four times the resolution in the longitudinal (z) direction, and over four times the brightness of AMATERAS-1.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical improvement based on optical principles.

claim: A 120-megapixel CMOS camera with a pixel size of 2.2 µm was used in AMATERAS-2.
source: We utilized either a 120-megapixel CMOS camera or a 250-megapixel CMOS camera, depending on the research purpose. Both the cameras have an approximately 35 mm diagonal, thus providing an observation FOV of 17.8 mm and 17.4 mm diagonal at ×2 magnification, respectively. The pixel sizes for these cameras are 2.2 and 1.5 µm, with sampling intervals of 1.1 and 0.75 µm at ×2 magnification, respectively.
evidence: The camera specifications are explicitly stated.

claim: A 250-megapixel CMOS camera with a pixel size of 1.5 µm was used in AMATERAS-2.
source: We utilized either a 120-megapixel CMOS camera or a 250-megapixel CMOS camera, depending on the research purpose. Both the cameras have an approximately 35 mm diagonal, thus providing an observation FOV of 17.8 mm and 17.4 mm diagonal at ×2 magnification, respectively. The pixel sizes for these cameras are 2.2 and 1.5 µm, with sampling intervals of 1.1 and 0.75 µm at ×2 magnification, respectively.
evidence: The camera specifications are explicitly stated.

claim: The transverse resolution obtained with the 120-megapixel camera was 1.24±0.12 µm (N=100).
source: The transverse resolutions (xy-direction) obtained with the 120- and 250-megapixel cameras were 1.24±0.12 (N=100) and 1.12±0.072 (N=100; Figure 2A–B, right top)
evidence: This is an experimental measurement stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The transverse resolution obtained with the 250-megapixel camera was 1.12±0.072 µm (N=100).
source: The transverse resolutions (xy-direction) obtained with the 120- and 250-megapixel cameras were 1.24±0.12 (N=100) and 1.12±0.072 (N=100; Figure 2A–B, right top)
evidence: This is an experimental measurement stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The DOF was measured to be 15.6±1.3 µm (N=100) for the 120-megapixel camera.
source: The DOF was measured to be 15.6±1.3 (N=100) and 14.8±1.1 (N=100) for the 120- and 250-megapixel cameras, respectively.
evidence: This is an experimental measurement stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The DOF was measured to be 14.8±1.1 µm (N=100) for the 250-megapixel camera.
source: The DOF was measured to be 15.6±1.3 (N=100) and 14.8±1.1 (N=100) for the 120- and 250-megapixel cameras, respectively.
evidence: This is an experimental measurement stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The difference in DOF between the two cameras is attributed to the distinct pixel sizes of the cameras.
source: This difference in DOF is attributed to the distinct pixel sizes of the cameras (Gross et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an interpretation with a supporting citation.

claim: The spatial resolution in the transverse direction has been significantly improved, approximately two times compared with that of AMATERAS-1.
source: The spatial resolution in the transverse direction has been significantly improved, approximately two times compared with that of AMATERAS-1.
evidence: This is a comparison between the two systems.

claim: AMATERAS-2w delivers more detailed images with finer spatial structures compared to AMATERAS-1.
source: Evidently, AMATERAS-2w delivers more detailed images with finer spatial structures.
evidence: This is stated in the text and demonstrated in Figure 2D-F.

claim: The filamentous actin stained with Rhodamine exhibits a sharper spatial resolution with AMATERAS-2w compared to AMATERAS-1.
source: This is further confirmed by the line profiles depicted in Figure 2F, where the filamentous actin stained with Rhodamine exhibits a sharper spatial resolution with AMATERAS-2w.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The imaging system enables observation of subcellular structures, such as myofibrils, in cell sheets with a large area.
source: This result indicated the capability of observing subcellular structures, such as myofibrils, in cell sheets with a large area, such as artificial myocardial sheets, which would enable us to simultaneously investigate microscale structures and macroscale multicellular dynamics.
evidence: This is stated as a capability demonstrated by the results.

claim: Light-sheet microscopy struggles with uniform illumination over the centimeter scale FOV of AMATERAS.
source: This is because the light-sheet microscopy struggles with uniform illumination over the centimeter scale FOV of AMATERAS (Battistella et al., 2022; Voigt et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated as a reason for not choosing light-sheet microscopy, with supporting citations.

claim: Light-field microscopy involves a trade-off between spatial resolution and the ability to resolve three dimensions, which is incompatible with AMATERAS's concept.
source: and the light-field microscopy involves a trade-off between spatial resolution and the ability to resolve three dimensions, which is incompatible with the AMATERAS's concept (Nöbauer et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as a reason for not choosing light-field microscopy, with a supporting citation.

claim: Two-photon excitation microscopy is crucial for deep tissue imaging, but still requires further innovations in pulsed laser power and scanning methods to be effectively applied to the wide FOV of AMATERAS.
source: In addition, two-photon excitation microscopy, including that using spatiotemporal focusing, is crucial for deep tissue imaging, but still requires further innovations in pulsed laser power and scanning methods to be effectively applied to the wide FOV of AMATERAS.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of two-photon microscopy for this application.

claim: The confocal method was considered the most compatible with the AMATERAS-2 imaging system.
source: We considered the confocal method to be the most compatible with our imaging system.
evidence: This is stated as the rationale for the chosen approach.

claim: The commonly used method involving a combination of a microlens array and a pinhole array disk could not be employed in AMATERAS owing to the large NA of the tube lens (NA=0.125) compared with that of standard microscopes.
source: The commonly used method involving a combination of a microlens array and a pinhole array disk (Ichihara et al., 1996; Ishihara, 2003) could not be employed in AMATERAS owing to the large NA of the tube lens (NA=0.125) compared with that of standard microscopes.
evidence: This is stated as a technical challenge with supporting citations.

claim: A custom-made pinhole array disk with pinhole size of 6 µm and spacing of 24 µm was designed for AMATERAS-2.
source: As a prototype, we set the pinhole size to 6 µm (Figure 3A), matching the Airy disk diameter for red wavelength. A more detailed discussion on the impact of pinhole diameter dependence on 3D resolution is available in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 (see also Appendix File - Note 1). The pinhole spacing was set as 24 µm, striking a balance between throughput and crosstalk (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The presence of the pinhole-array disk dramatically suppressed background light from outside the focal plane.
source: The presence of the pinhole-array disk dramatically suppressed background light from outside the focal plane.
evidence: This is stated in the text and demonstrated in Figure 3C.

claim: Optical sectioning can be achieved by the pinhole-array disk.
source: This verified that optical sectioning can be achieved by the pinhole-array disk.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: The transverse spatial resolution with the ×1 relay lens is degraded compared to the one obtained by the wide-field configuration without the relay lens.
source: As NA of the ×1 relay lens (NA=0.079) is lower than that of the tube lens (NA=0.125), the transverse spatial resolution (Figure 3D, right top) is degraded compared to the one obtained by the wide-field configuration without the relay lens (Figure 2A and B, Appendix File - Note 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to figures.

claim: The ×2 relay lens (NA=0.12) almost matches with the tube lens, and the reduction in the transverse spatial resolution is relatively small.
source: By contrast, the ×2 relay lens (NA=0.12) almost matches with the tube lens, and the reduction in the transverse spatial resolution is relatively small (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3E.

claim: The FWHM of the PSF in the longitudinal direction was approximately 16 µm with a ×1 relay lens and approximately 14 µm with a ×2 relay lens.
source: As for the longitudinal resolution, the FWHM of the PSF was approximately 16 µm with a ×1 relay lens and approximately 14 µm with a ×2 relay lens, both values significantly exceeding the ideal value about 9.5 µm (Appendix File - Note 1).
evidence: This is stated as experimental measurements with reference to figures.

claim: The discrepancies between measured and ideal longitudinal resolution are attributed to the relatively loose focusing of the excitation light and the non-negligible size of the pinhole.
source: These discrepancies are attributed to the relatively loose focusing of the excitation light and the non-negligible size of the pinhole.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: A computational sectioning method was developed to separate images of the focal plane and out-of-focal planes.
source: In addition to optical sectioning, we developed a computational sectioning method to separate images of the focal plane and out-of-focal planes.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological development.

claim: The computational sectioning method estimates the contribution from out-of-focus planes as the baseline by iteratively applying low-pass filtering under the assumption that the image's spatial frequency in the focal plane is higher than that in out-of-focus planes.
source: We estimated the contribution from out-of-focus planes as the baseline by iteratively applying low-pass filtering under the assumption that the image's spatial frequency in the focal plane is higher than that in out-of-focus planes.
evidence: This is stated as the principle of the computational method.

claim: After computational sectioning, the distribution of cTnT and nuclei in each z-layer is clearly visualized.
source: After the sectioning, the distribution of cTnT and nuclei in each z-layer is clearly visualized (Figure 4D)
evidence: This is stated as a result and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The hollow oval structure of the myocardial organoid is formed by a thin layer of cTnT-positive cells (cardiomyocytes) whereas the underlying cell layer is composed of cTnT-negative cells.
source: A 3D isosurface representation (Figure 4E) shows that the hollow oval structure is formed by a thin layer of cTnT-positive cells (cardiomyocytes) whereas the underlying cell layer is composed of cTnT-negative cells, consistent with previous literature (Ma et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4E and supporting citation.

claim: The computational sectioning method is effective in cellular imaging when fluorescent molecules are localized within the cell or exhibit a filament-like structure.
source: This method is effective in cellular imaging when fluorescent molecules are localized within the cell, like in the nucleus, or when they exhibit a filament-like structure, thereby enabling cell recognition and dynamic tracking.
evidence: This is stated as a condition for the method's effectiveness.

claim: The computational sectioning method relies on the spatial frequency of the fluorescence image in the focal plane being uniform and clearly higher than that outside the focal plane.
source: It relies on the spatial frequency of the fluorescence image in the focal plane being uniform and clearly higher than that outside the focal plane.
evidence: This is stated as a principle underlying the method.

claim: Imaging of a 1.5-mm-thick mouse brain section was performed using AMATERAS-2.
source: To demonstrate the potential for brain imaging, we performed imaging of a 1.5-mm-thick mouse brain section in the coronal plane (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental demonstration with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: The brain was chemically cleared using CUBIC.
source: The brain was chemically cleared using CUBIC (Susaki et al., 2014; Tainaka et al., 2018), and the cell nuclei were stained with SYTOX-Green (Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a sample preparation method with supporting citations.

claim: A total of 378 layers were acquired to cover the entire 1.5-mm-thick volume in steps of 4 µm in the z-direction.
source: Each layer's exposure time was 1 s, and a total of 378 layers were acquired to cover the entire 1.5-mm-thick volume in steps of 4 µm in the z-direction.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental parameter.

claim: By utilizing computational sectioning to eliminate background light, clear images were obtained even in areas with strong background light.
source: By utilizing computational sectioning to eliminate background light, clear images were obtained even in areas with strong background light.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the computational method.

claim: The higher magnification (×4) allows for improved spatial resolution and separation of individual cells in both the xy and xz planes compared to ×2 magnification.
source: A comparison of the images at ×2 and ×4 magnification in Figure 5E and F reveals that the higher magnification (×4) allows for improved spatial resolution and separation of individual cells in both the xy and xz planes.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figures 5E and F.

claim: ELEPHANT is an interactive platform for cell detection and tracking that seamlessly integrates manual annotation with deep learning and allows for result proofreading.
source: For cell detection in the 3D imaging data of the mouse brain section, we used a recently developed interactive platform for cell detection and tracking, called ELEPHANT (Efficient LEarning using sParse Human Annotations for Nuclear Tracking; Sugawara et al., 2022). This platform seamlessly integrates manual annotation with deep learning and allows for result proofreading (Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the analysis tool with citation.

claim: The precision and recall of the cell detection in the cortex were estimated to be 99.4% and 97.6%, respectively.
source: The precision and recall of the cell detection were estimated to be 99.4% and 97.6 %, respectively (Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative evaluation of the cell detection performance.

claim: The cell density in the cortex was calculated to be 1.18×10^5 cells/mm^3, which closely matches previous reports.
source: Based on these results, the cell density in the cortex was calculated to be 1.18×105 cells/mm3, which closely matches previous reports (Herculano-Houzel and Lent, 2005).
evidence: This is stated as a calculated result with supporting citation.

claim: Time-lapse fluorescence imaging of the quail embryo began at 36 hr (HH10) after the start of egg incubation and captured eYFP signals in the developing embryo for 25 hr.
source: Time-lapse fluorescence imaging began at 36 hr (HH10) after the start of egg incubation and captured eYFP signals in the developing embryo for 25 hr.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental parameter.

claim: For 3D imaging of the quail embryo, z-stacks were acquired every 7.5 min, with each z-stack containing 21 layers spaced 12 µm apart.
source: For 3D imaging, we acquired z-stacks every 7.5 min, with each z-stack containing 21 layers spaced 12 µm apart.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental parameter.

claim: The intensity density of the excitation light was 113 mW/cm² at the sample plane, and the exposure time per layer was 1 s.
source: The intensity density of the excitation light was 113 mW/cm² at the sample plane, and the exposure time per layer was 1 s, under which conditions the quail embryo developed normally without significant phototoxicity or photobleaching.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental parameter.

claim: Under the imaging conditions used, the quail embryo developed normally without significant phototoxicity or photobleaching.
source: The intensity density of the excitation light was 113 mW/cm² at the sample plane, and the exposure time per layer was 1 s, under which conditions the quail embryo developed normally without significant phototoxicity or photobleaching.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the experimental conditions.

claim: The time-lapse 3D imaging of the quail embryo yielded a total of 4200 image layers (21 layers ×200 time points) with a data size of approximately 500 GB.
source: This time-lapse 3D imaging yielded a total of 4200 image layers (21 layers ×200 time points) with a data size of approximately 500 GB.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the data generated.

claim: Approximately 4.5×10^6 cells were detected across all 200 time points in the quail embryo imaging.
source: Segmentation of cell nuclei allowed us to detect approximately 4.5×106 cells across all 200 time points
evidence: This is stated as a result of the cell detection analysis.

claim: About 4.0×10^5 cells were tracked by linking cells in close proximity over consecutive time points in the quail embryo imaging.
source: and by linking cells in close proximity over consecutive time points, we tracked about 4.0×105 cells.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the cell tracking analysis.

claim: The distribution of high meandering index at t=8 hr and 16 hr was significantly changed in the quail embryo.
source: We found that the distribution of high meandering index at t=8 hr and 16 hr was significantly changed.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figures 6F and G.

claim: The FOV-to-spatial resolution ratio of AMATERAS-2 surpasses those of previously reported large-FOV imaging methods.
source: Notably, this FOV-to-spatial resolution ratio surpasses those of previously reported large-FOV imaging methods.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous methods.

claim: The optical invariant of AMATERAS-2 has a value of 2.75.
source: The key metric 'optical invariant', derived from the product of NA and FOV, has a value of 2.75 (Materials and methods, Bumstead et al., 2018), thus indicating excellent performance of the lens system.
evidence: This is stated as a calculated metric with citation.

claim: The space-bandwidth product of AMATERAS-2 reaches 4.3×10^8.
source: Furthermore, the 'space-bandwidth product', which signifies the FOV to spatial resolution ratio achieved under real measurement conditions (considering image sensor size and wavelength), reaches 4.3×108 (Materials and methods, Lohmann et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated as a calculated metric with citation.

claim: Both the optical invariant and space-bandwidth product of AMATERAS-2 significantly outperform those reported in earlier studies on large FOV imaging methods.
source: Both of these metrics significantly outperform those reported in earlier studies on large FOV imaging methods (McConnell et al., 2016; Sofroniew et al., 2016; Fan et al., 2019; Ota et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2021; Bumstead et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous methods with supporting citations.

claim: The spatial resolution (FWHM) of AMATERAS-2w and –2c was measured to be approximately 1.1–1.8 μm in the transverse direction (xy) and 13–16 μm in the longitudinal direction (z).
source: The spatial resolution (FWHM) of AMATERAS-2w and –2 c was measured to be approximately 1.1–1.8 μm in the transverse direction (xy) and 13–16 μm in the longitudinal direction (z) through PSF measurements (Figures 2A, B, 3D and E).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of experimental measurements with reference to figures.

claim: The spatial resolution of AMATERAS-2 represents a significant enhancement compared with the previous AMATERAS version (2.3 and 64 µm, respectively).
source: These values represent a significant enhancement compared with the previous AMATERAS version (2.3 and 64 µm, respectively; Ichimura et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with the previous version with citation.

claim: The improved transverse resolution enables clearer visualization of intracellular filamentous structures.
source: The improved transverse resolution enables clearer visualization of intracellular filamentous structures (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated as a result with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: The refinement in longitudinal resolution was more than four times greater, demonstrating that the expected effect was achieved with more than double NA.
source: Moreover, the refinement in longitudinal resolution was more than four times greater, thus demonstrating that the expected effect was achieved with more than double NA.
evidence: This is stated as an evaluation of the improvement.

claim: Volumetric imaging of a 1.5-mm-thick mouse brain coronal section was successfully achieved using the multipoint-scanning confocal imaging method, along with computational sectioning and tissue-clearing.
source: We successfully achieved volumetric imaging of a 1.5-mm-thick mouse brain coronal section using the multipoint-scanning confocal imaging method, along with computational sectioning and tissue-clearing (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated as a result with reference to Figure 5.

claim: The exposure time per image for the mouse brain section was 1 s, and data acquisition took less than 10 min.
source: The exposure time per image was 1 s, and data acquisition took less than 10 min.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental parameter.

claim: Previous methods such as light-sheet imaging and block-face serial microscopy tomography require half a day or more for whole-brain data acquisition owing to tiling images from a narrow FOV.
source: Unlike previous methods such as light-sheet imaging (Susaki et al., 2014) and block-face serial microscopy tomography (Seiriki et al., 2019), which require half a day or more for whole-brain data acquisition owing to tiling images from a narrow FOV, our method can significantly reduce the acquisition time when extended to the whole brain.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous methods with supporting citations.

claim: AMATERAS-2 can significantly reduce the acquisition time for whole-brain imaging when extended to the whole brain.
source: Unlike previous methods such as light-sheet imaging (Susaki et al., 2014) and block-face serial microscopy tomography (Seiriki et al., 2019), which require half a day or more for whole-brain data acquisition owing to tiling images from a narrow FOV, our method can significantly reduce the acquisition time when extended to the whole brain.
evidence: This is stated as a potential advantage of the method.

claim: AMATERAS-2 can perform time-lapse observation of the centimeter-sized vascular networks in the quail embryo.
source: We have shown that AMATERAS-2 can perform time-lapse observation of the centimeter-sized vascular networks in the quail embryo.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability.

claim: AMATERAS-2 is a promising tool for understanding the multicellular behavior, especially the mechanisms of tissue formation during development.
source: It is a promising tool for understanding the multicellular behavior, especially the mechanisms of tissue formation during development (Sasai, 2013; McDole et al., 2018; Dominguez et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as a potential application with supporting citations.

claim: The data obtained from the quail embryo are the first demonstration of the dynamics of the extensive organization of the vascular network throughout the quail embryo at the single-cell level.
source: In regard to the quail embryo's case, the data obtained here are the first demonstration of the dynamics of the extensive organization of the vascular network throughout the quail embryo at the single-cell level.
